description: Feverfew is a bushy short-lived perennial herb with small daisy-like flowers, used traditionally to prevent migraines and reduce fever. It self-seeds freely and grows easily in full sun to part shade. The bitter, aromatic leaves are the medicinal part, taken fresh or dried.

companions.notes: openfarm-crops-rescue lists this as a companion without indicating polarity; assumed 'good' per common convention

data_sources.notes: growth_habit='upright' inferred by Ollama (Trefle growth_habit is bare 'Forb/herb' - ambiguous between upright/rosette/spreading, deferred to Ollama); reasoning: Feverfew is described as a bushy herb, which indicates it grows in an upright clump.
life_cycle='perennial' inferred by Ollama; reasoning: Feverfew is typically grown as a short-lived perennial in home gardens in Belgium.
edible_parts=['leaves'] inferred by Ollama; reasoning: The description mentions that the leaves are the medicinal part and can be taken fresh or dried.

is_edible corrected from false to true (GitHub issue #165): edible_parts=['leaves'] was already populated, a direct contradiction with is_edible=false, and no is_toxic flag or toxicity_notes explained the discrepancy - a full-dataset audit found this affecting 120 plants (grown from an earlier 25-plant spot-check once backlog #133's edible_parts backfill widened coverage), all of them unambiguous real food/herb/fruit crops.
